sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface display confirmed by anti-FLAG immunofluorescence in transfected HEK293T cells; phosphatase activity or trafficking efficiency NOT MEASURED relative to untagged control.
sites.rationale: PTPRA is a type I single-pass transmembrane protein with exactly one extracellular terminus: the mature N-terminus beginning at residue 20 (after signal-peptide cleavage at residue 19). Anti-FLAG surface staining (L3) confirms the FLAG tag is extracellular; topology forces it to this sole extracellular terminus, giving insert_after_residue=19 by the topology_derived rule. Python confirms residue 19 is A and residue 20 is N, 132 residues from the TM boundary. The constructs were custom-generated (not a commercial plasmid with unstated position), so topology derivation is valid. Custom V5/FLAG-tagged full-length RPTPα WT and R223W constructs were generated and expressed in HEK293T cells; anti-FLAG immunofluorescence confirmed plasma membrane surface display of the FLAG tag (L3). No residue is stated for the tag junction.

sources.claim: (C) Immunofluorescent image of transfected HEK293T cells stained with anti-FLAG antibody.

sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Bivalent anti-HA antibody activated HARPTPalpha-EGFR chimeras (dimerisation-dependent EGFR kinase activation confirmed), demonstrating surface accessibility of the HA tag; endogenous RPTPalpha phosphatase activity in the chimera context NOT MEASURED.
sites.rationale: The chimera is a membrane-anchored full-length transmembrane protein (RPTPalpha ectodomain + EGFR TM/ICD), not a secreted ectodomain, so it qualifies under the ledger rules. The HA tag is placed somewhere within the ectodomain (residues 20–151); because no residue is named and the tag could be at the N-terminus or internal, the site is reported at region level with insert_after_residue null. The chimera system functionally validated surface display via antibody-induced dimerisation. Ranked second because the junction is unresolved and the construct is a chimera rather than full-length RPTPalpha. HA-epitope-tagged RPTPalpha ectodomain (residues 20–151) was fused to the EGFR transmembrane and intracellular domain to create a membrane-anchored chimera (HARPTPalpha-EGFR); bivalent anti-HA antibody activated the chimera, demonstrating surface exposure of the HA tag in the ectodomain. No specific residue junction is named in the paper.

sources.claim: We developed a system to study the function of the ectodomain of RPTPalpha, a transmembrane protein-tyrosine phosphatase, by fusing the HA-epitope tagged ectodomain of RPTPalpha to the transmembrane and intracellular domain of the epidermal growth factor receptor, EGFR, a receptor protein-tyrosine kinase that is activated by dimerization. Although the use of chemical crosslinkers shows that preformed HARPTPalpha-EGFR dimers exist, bivalent anti-HA-tag antibody activated HARPTPalpha-EGFR chimeras, suggesting this system may be used to study regulation of dimerization.

literature_notes: L2 (V5/FLAG constructs generated for stability/trafficking study) and L3 (anti-FLAG surface immunofluorescence) are treated as a single evidence pair grounded in L3, the more informative clip. L4 (C-terminal twin-strep-tag and YFP fusions on full-length PTPRA) is placed in other_positions because the C-terminus (residue 802) lies within the intracellular domain (173–802). The ectodomain site from L1 cannot be pinned to a residue because the paper names only 'ectodomain' without a junction residue, and the tag could be at the N-terminus or at an internal loop; it is therefore reported as a region-level site. No ledger line names a specific residue for any extracellular insertion in PTPRA, so no 'validated' site exists.

literature_other_positions.note: Full-length PTPRA was fused to a twin-strep-tag or YFP at the C-terminus (residue 802); the C-terminus lies within the intracellular domain (173–802) and is not surface-accessible.
